claim: Let a finite group \(G\) act isometrically on a compact metric space \((X,d)\), and let a continuous \(G\)-equivariant map \(f:X\to X\) induce \(T:X/G\to X/G\). For the set-valued map \(F(x)=Gf(x)\), ordinary shadowing and periodic shadowing are each equivalent, with identical admissible \((\delta,\varepsilon)\) pairs, to the corresponding property of \(T\) in the quotient metric. Moreover, \(F^n(x)=\pi^{-1}(T^n\pi x)\), so its period-dividing-\(n\) point counts are weighted by orbit-fibre size. Positive expansivity of \(F\) implies that of \(T\); the converse holds for free actions, but fails for an explicit two-sheet Cantor wedge whose quotient is the one-sided binary full shift. In that nonfree example both maps have shadowing and periodic shadowing, yet only the quotient is positively expansive, and the set-valued periodic-point zeta equals \((1-z)/(1-2z)^2\).
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: The exact reduction concerns orbit-saturated finite isometric group actions, not arbitrary multifunctions. Free action is sufficient but not claimed necessary for reverse expansivity. The formal point-count zeta counts states with an n-step return, not multiple path realizations. All conclusions are proved analytically; no independent external verification is claimed.
title: Exact shadowing reduction and a branching obstruction for finite-symmetry multivalued dynamics
